reason: Reproduced exactly, by real Tab presses rather than a scripted focus, so it is not an artifact of programmatic focus. Chromium, ?v=light&state=full, 1440x960: seven Tabs reach the strip, four more land on the fifth mark, and the browser's own minimal scroll-into-view parks it flush at the fold (top 948, bottom 960, .scroll scrollTop 4) with the tip on. Resize with nothing else touched: 1280x844 leaves the mark at top 948 in an 844 window (104px below), 768x1024 at 1457 (433px below, in a viewport TALLER than the one it was focused in, so this is content reflow, not window shrink), 390x844 at 1570 (726px below). In all three document.activeElement is still that mark, tip.classList 'on' is gone, scrollTop never moves off 4. Nothing in the source restores it: grep across lately.html finds no scroll-margin, no focusin, no focus() and no scrollIntoView anywhere, and the only repaint path is :1072. The behaviour gate never resizes with focus held, so this is not a restatement of it; the class is named in the defect library at lessons.md:265 and it is back through the one path the surface has. Two corrections to the seat's write-up, neither fatal. First, the headline consequence is overstated: driven at 390x844, tabbing to a mark scrolls .scroll to 1158 and puts it mid-viewport, and rotating to 844x390 and back keeps it in view (top 303 of 390, then 420 of 844) with the tip still on. The phone-rotation story does not reproduce on its own. What does reproduce is the arrival state -- the first Tab onto the strip always leaves the mark knife-edged at the fold, and any resize from there strands it -- which is common enough to carry the finding without the rotation claim. Second, severity: defect is the right class and is not overstated. The surface still does what it says and asserts nothing untrue; a keyboard or magnifier reader silently loses the ring and the mark's title, which lives nowhere else on this screen. The fix is correct as written: root is in scope at :1072, .scroll has no scroll-behavior: smooth so scrollIntoView lands instantly, and the seat's claim about ordering holds -- onMove does not clear `showing` on the out-of-view branch, so the queueMove rAF fires after the scroll and re-places the tip against the restored position. Patched in and re-driven, the same three resizes return the mark to view with the tip on (top 832/844, 1012/1024, 832/844).
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's handler as written, with one addition. block: "nearest" parks the mark flush against the viewport bottom -- measured at 1280x844 and 390x844 the restored mark sits at top 832, bottom 844 -- and .dot:focus-visible is a 2px outline at outline-offset: 3px, so the bottom 5px of the ring is clipped off-screen. Add `scroll-margin-block: 12px` to the `.dot` rule (lately.html:348) so "nearest" leaves room for the ring; that also improves the browser's own tab-arrival scroll, which produces the same knife-edge today (948/960 at 1440x960) and is the state this whole finding starts from. Do not switch to block: "center" -- it yanks the reader further than the move that displaced them. Final handler at :1072: window.addEventListener("resize", () => { const held = document.activeElement; relayout(); if (held && held !== document.body && root.contains(held)) { const b = held.getBoundingClientRect(); if (b.top < 0 || b.bottom > window.innerHeight) held.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }); } queueMove(); });
breaks: The fix introduces the surface's first programmatic scroll, so three things need re-measuring. (1) Touch pins. onMove drops a pinned tip whose mark has left the viewport; because queueMove's rAF now runs after the scrollIntoView, a pin that would have been dropped on resize survives instead. That is the better behaviour but it is a change -- re-run interaction-check.mjs:1206 ("a pinned label is dismissed or follows its mark"), which is scroll-driven and should be untouched, and add a resize case beside it. (2) Entrance and count-up. A resize during the hero count-up or the reveal now moves the scroll container mid-animation; drive ?motion=play at each width with focus held and confirm nothing stutters or double-fires. (3) The de-swarm ordering. relayout() must stay before the measurement, as the seat has it -- reading getBoundingClientRect before deswarm() has re-rowed the marks would scroll to the pre-reflow position. Also re-run the audit gate: scroll-margin-block on .dot touches no palette, weight, family, contrast, hit-target, radius, motion or type-ramp assertion, but the hit-target check reads .dot boxes and should be confirmed unchanged.
